info.title: OpenAsy Alerts API
info.summary: Alerts grouped, routed to the team that owns them, silenced for maintenance and sent to whoever is on call.
info.description:
Every screen of alerts uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only; anything removed is deprecated first (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Send alerts with `ALERTS_INGEST_TOKEN`, to `/api/v1/alerts` or, from Prometheus, to Alertmanager's `/api/v2/alerts`. Everything else takes the session of a signed-in person or an API token, and each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`: viewer, editor, admin; ADR 0003).

Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

post.description: For products and scripts: a list of alerts, or an Alertmanager webhook's `{ alerts }`, optionally gzipped. Send an alert again while it holds; it resolves at its endsAt, or after the resolve timeout. With `ALERTS_INGEST_TOKEN`, or an API token with the editor role.

post.summary: Send alerts, as to an Alertmanager
post.description:
Alertmanager's own path, so Prometheus and vmalert can name alerts as their Alertmanager:

```yaml
alerting:
  alertmanagers:
    - scheme: https
      authorization: { credentials: <ALERTS_INGEST_TOKEN> }
      static_configs: [{ targets: [alerts.example.com] }]
```

get.description: Needs the viewer role. Firing first, with the alerts resolved in the last hour.

put.description: Needs the editor role. Repeats and escalation stop until a new alert joins the group.

post.description: Needs the editor role. A silence stops notifications, never the alerts: they stay on the screens.

delete.description: Needs the editor role. It stays in the list as expired.

200.description: The schedules, with who is on call.

post.description: Needs the editor role. Members take turns of shiftHours each.

delete.description: Needs the editor role. Not while a route uses it.

post.description: Needs the admin role: a webhook's address is a secret.

delete.description: Needs the admin role. Not while a route sends to it.

get.description: Needs the viewer role. The newest 200.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` when alerts runs on plain http://localhost). Requests that change something must come from the alerts origin.

apiToken.description: An API token created under Settings → API tokens (`oa_alerts_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

adminToken.description: Only when alerts is started by its tests or a local script: one shared token with the admin role. A production install does not have it.

ingestToken.description: `ALERTS_INGEST_TOKEN`: for Prometheus, products and scripts. It can send alerts, nothing else.

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

id.description: The product, as OpenAsy names it.

url.description: The address people open it at.

PostableAlert.description: An alert as Prometheus sends one to an Alertmanager.

labels.description: What the alert is; the same labels are the same alert.

annotations.description: What people read: summary, description, runbook_url.

endsAt.description: When it resolves. Without one it resolves after the resolve timeout unless sent again.

status.description: From an Alertmanager webhook; resolved ends the alert now.

value.description: A regular expression for =~ and !~, anchored at both ends.

mention.description: A Slack user or group id, to mention them; empty for none.

route.description: Null when no route takes it: nobody is told.

labels.description: The values of the route's group labels.

silenced.description: Firing alerts it holds back now.

endsAt.description: At most 30 days after it starts.

startsAt.description: When the first member's first shift starts; now when left out.

target.description: Where it posts, without the secret part of the address.

kind.description: slack: an incoming webhook; teams: a workflow that posts a card it is sent; webhook: the whole group as JSON.

url.description: Kept sealed with the install's key; never shown again in full.

routes.description: In order: the first route whose matchers all match an alert takes it. A route with no matchers takes everything left.

id.description: Keep a route's id when sending it again.
